text: Start with the denominator. A survey of managers around the world, a sample of US spending-platform customers, and a representative US business survey describe different populations. Their percentages cannot be averaged into a global adoption rate. A difference between them is not evidence that one source is wrong. Then check what the measure can see. A company could use a free AI tool without an observed payment. It could pay for a subscription that staff rarely use. A team could run AI in production while most of the company has made no change. These situations belong at different stages of adoption. Finally, align the period and the question. A monthly payment measure and a two-week use measure are not interchangeable. Changes in the question, supplier coverage, or customer sample can change a series even when behavior has not changed by the same amount. The 2026 report's business analysis examines spending intensity, inference economics, and how companies change their workflows. This reference complements that annual snapshot by comparing measurement methods across sources.
